gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each Samsung pick costs once you add Samsung's own keyboard cover. On samsung.com on 2026-11-10 the totals were: Galaxy Tab S10 FE 128 GB $549.99 + Book Cover Keyboard (AI Key) $199.99 = $749.98; Galaxy Tab S11 $999.99 + Book Cover Keyboard Slim $144.99 = $1,144.98; Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra 256 GB $1,299.99 + Book Cover Keyboard Slim $209.99 = $1,509.98. On the S10 FE, the keyboard adds 36% to the tablet price.
standout_why: I compared against MyNextTablet's 'The 8 Best Tablets With a Keyboard: 2026 Edition' (cited, opened 2026-11-10). It lists the S10 Lite, S10 FE, S10 FE+, S11 and S11 Ultra, says each one's Book Cover Keyboard is sold separately, and gives no tablet price, no keyboard price and no total. ChatGPT itself said 'compare the total price' but gave no totals. Its S11 card showed $899.99, while samsung.com shows $999.99 today. I could not read the cited Samsung government MSRP PDF: WebFetch returned only compressed binary and local PDF tools needed approval. It may list keyboard MSRPs, so I scored this 2, not 3. Wired could not be fetched. I did not open the other uncited top results (Android Authority, Tech Advisor, LaptopBee).
decides: This keeps the S10 FE as the value pick, but the real cost with a keyboard is $749.98, not the $549.99 tablet price. The FE's own keyboard ($199.99) costs more than the S11's Slim cover ($144.99), so the gap between the two shrinks from $450 for the tablets alone to $395 with keyboards. The S11 Ultra with a keyboard comes to $1,509.98, which takes it out of a 'Budget including keyboard: Over $1,000' bucket that ChatGPT priced from the $1,299.99 tablet alone. Samsung's current US keyboard page is titled for both the Tab S12 Ultra and the S11 Ultra, so the S11 Ultra is no longer Samsung's newest Ultra.
